rationale: Investigate the actual in-repository Ready/application consumer for the unresolved early-Advance premise; retain what this helper establishes without converting its stricter schedule into a public contract.

feedback.answered: InteractionEnv.ProcessReady takes a Ready, performs processAppend and processApply synchronously in normal mode, queues outgoing messages, and only then calls Advance. processApply decodes each committed configuration and calls RawNode.ApplyConfChange before recording its corresponding state-machine history snapshot. In async mode ProcessReady only queues worker work; ProcessApplyThread removes the first apply message, completes processApply, then queues its saved responses. Thus this actual helper preserves membership application before acknowledgment in both modes and cannot expose an Advance-before-ApplyConfChange history without a deliberate different driver. This is a concrete narrower implementation policy, not evidence that every order permitted by Node.Advance is forbidden.
remaining: Resolve whether Node.Advance permitting application overlap includes configuration callbacks themselves; current helper usage supplies no affirmative authority for that input.
If such overlap is independently justified, construct a distinct compliant Node/API schedule rather than weakening or reusing this helper policy.
The configuration-triggered read-release lead still requires a legal history and a responsibility beyond permitted read-request loss.
feedback.rationale: Reading both the Ready consumer and its application callee answers the helper-ownership premise. Normal-mode behavior and async completion ordering are kept distinct; no execution or result from the completed failed-transfer check is reused.
